Article Title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi

PM Modi stresses packaging, highlights traditional skills

Heval river rejuvenation , e-Sanjeevani consultations highlighted

PM calls 12-year journey of Mann Ki Baat a ‘pilgrimage’

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged people to prioritise products made by local artisans while shopping for festivals, saying their purchases would strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ campaign and help realise the vision of a self-reliant India.Addressing the 139th edition of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat , PM Modi said the campaign was helping Indian products reach international markets, citing the export of makhana from Bihar to Greece and arhar dal from Karnataka to the Maldives.The prime minister noted that people typically purchase gifts and other items for their families and loved ones during festivals, and called on them to support local artisans through their shopping choices.“This time too, while shopping, please give priority to products made by local artisans. Your purchases will boost their enthusiasm,” he said.PM Modi said greater participation in the ‘Vocal for Local’ campaign would accelerate the progress towards a self-reliant India.“Therefore, I personally urge you to give priority and prominence to products crafted by local artisans,” he added.The prime minister also emphasised the importance of packaging in attracting consumers and helping products find a place in the market.“Often, when we see something in the market, good packaging makes us pick it up, and we want to learn more about the product. Understanding this, greater emphasis is now being laid on packaging,” he said.During the broadcast, PM Modi also highlighted efforts to revive traditional skills and farming practices, including an initiative to promote natural cotton cultivation in Punjab’s Malwa region.He said the organisation Kheti Virasat Mission had been working to revive organic farming and had launched an initiative called ‘Nav-Trinjan’ to encourage natural cotton farming.The initiative also started a weaving school a few years ago to pass the traditional skill on to younger generations.“You can imagine how great a help this is for the environment. Friends, a few years ago, 'Nav-Trinjan' also started a weaving school with the goal of passing on the skill of weaving to the new generation,” PM Modi said.PM Modi also spoke about efforts by residents and the local administration in Uttarakhand’s Tehri Garhwal district to revive the Heval river.He said the river’s water level had begun to fall some time ago, while natural water sources in the surrounding areas were drying up. In response, villagers and the administration launched conservation efforts that included rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and large-scale tree planting.“Today, these efforts have given the Heval river a new lease of life while also helping rejuvenate dozens of natural water sources,” the prime minister said.He also highlighted the use of technology in healthcare through the e-Sanjeevani telemedicine service, which enables people to access medical consultations remotely.“It brings me immense satisfaction to share that nearly 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted through it so far. This is a massive figure and a prime example of the power of technology, the service-mindedness of our doctors, and the trust of our citizens,” he said.PM Modi added that the service’s extensive network enabled it to reach even the most remote parts of the country, with beneficiaries’ experiences offering examples of its reach.The Sunday broadcast also marked 12 years of Mann Ki Baat. PM Modi described the programme’s journey as a “pilgrimage”, saying it had allowed him to learn about citizens’ efforts and acknowledge their contributions.“Since then, our journey has been continuing without interruption. You are both fellow travellers and guides on this journey,” he said, recalling that the programme began on Vijayadashami 12 years ago.The prime minister said the broadcast had given him an opportunity to highlight the hard work, courage, dedication and spirit of service shown by ordinary people across the country.“For me, Mann Ki Baat is no less than a pilgrimage to closely learn about the efforts of the people of the country and to bow down to their contributions,” he said.PM Modi added that the programme had brought attention to people whose work might otherwise go unnoticed and had allowed him to connect with families across India.He said he received hundreds of messages from listeners who told him that listening to Mann Ki Baat made them feel as though he were sitting among them and speaking as a member of their family. He described the affection expressed by listeners as an “invaluable asset”.
Article Summary: PM Modi stresses packaging, highlights traditional skills and farming practices. Heval river rejuvenation, e-Sanjeevani consultations highlighted. PM calls 12-year journey of Mann Ki Baat a ‘pilgrimage’Join conversation. Share your thoughts in the comments.

Article Title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises
Article Text:
EAM S Jaishankar urged the UN to lead efforts against global crises and terrorism, calling for multilateral reforms and inclusive AI development

Global South faces '4F crisis'

Jaishankar calls for inclusive AI development

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday urged the United Nations to take a stronger leadership role in tackling global crises, saying it must not remain a spectator to conflicts and other challenges facing the world.Speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on the occasion of UN Day, Jaishankar called for reforms in multilateral institutions, arguing that large parts of the world could not be excluded from decision-making.“The UN must show leadership, not be a spectator to global crises,” he said, adding that the case for reformed multilateralism was growing stronger by the day.Jaishankar also described terrorism as a major threat to global peace, rejecting its use as an instrument of statecraft.“Its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable. It can never be justified, it can never be rationalized,” he said, calling for stronger international resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms.The minister said some countries continued to allow political calculations to take precedence over the fight against terrorism, despite the lessons of history.Jaishankar highlighted the challenges confronting developing countries, describing the Global South as facing a “4F crisis” involving finance, fuel, food and fertiliser.He said developed countries also had a stake in finding solutions and called for urgent steps to reduce risks in the international economy and provide nations with more diversified options.“Market distortions through constriction and choke points only add to suffering. A genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue,” he said.On technological change, Jaishankar said artificial intelligence could transform the world but warned against leaving its development and impact in the hands of a few.“AI promises to be the mother of all change,” he said, arguing that such a far-reaching technology required a responsible, inclusive and human-centric approach.He said India supported a broader perspective on AI, given its universal applicability and potential consequences for societies worldwide.Jaishankar also stressed that progress and prosperity were inseparable, saying the world could not advance while large sections of humanity remained deprived.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday urged the United Nations to take a stronger leadership role in tackling global crises. He said the Global South was facing a ‘4F crisis’ involving finance, fuel, food and fertiliser. He also called for multilateral reforms and inclusive AI development.

Article Title: US asylum gamble blew gangster Himanshu Bhau’s cover: 'Used fake passport to evade global law'
Article Text:
Gangsters Himanshu Bhau (In black) and Neeraj Faridpuria in custody in US

Favourite route

‘Bhau used

fake passport

to evade global law’

Most-wanted gangster





NEW DELHI: A gamble to secure asylum in North America may have blown the cover of gangster Himanshu Bhau, one of north India’s notorious fugitives.A day after TOI reported his detention in Nevada, sources said a brief, staged detention in Feb by Bhau and his aide Neeraj Faridpuria, designed to exploit legal loopholes and claim asylum, backfired and unravelled the plan.The two face more than 25 criminal cases each across Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, including murder. Once the duo deliberately surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and details were fed into US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tracking system, which set off red flags.Sources said fugitives from India were aggressively seeking this modus operandi. Lawrence Bishnoi’s brother, Anmol, too had tried it but was busted.Currently lodged at the Henderson Detention Center under the jurisdiction of ICE, Bhau, sources said, used a forged passport under the alias Himanshu Singroha and evaded global law enforcement for over four years.However, his calculated scheme to get himself deliberately detained along with his chief associate, Neeraj Faridpuria, who also was using a fake passport under the name Neeraj Kaushik, triggered their detention.Once the duo deliberat-ely surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and personal details were fed into the ICE track-ing system. Picking up critical leads from this database entry, Indian law enforcement agencies and US security counterparts dug deeper into the background of “Himanshu Singroha”.Through cross-verification with local intelligen-ce sources, police contacts, and diplomatic counterparts, authorities confirmed that the individual in custody was indeed the high-profile fu­gitive Himanshu Bhau, a source said.The details on the ICE portal, accessed by TOI, corroborate the details, including the fake name on the passport. Investigations further revealed Faridpuria also shifted his base from Portugal to the US in late 2025 before reuniting with Bhau.The cops shared a dossier, including a photograph showing Faridpuria with guns and their other biometric details, which confirmed they were using forged documents. They were formally detained and information was shared with Indian agencies.The two are linked to the 2024 murder in South Delhi’s Aya Nagar in which over 70 bullets were fired, another recent connected killing, the 2019 murder of Congress leader Vikas Chaudhary in Faridabad, and a shooting outside YouTuber Elvish Yadav’s residence.Following confirmation of their detention in a Nevada prison, Indian agencies are working with US auth­orities to expedite their deportation. A special team is likely to be dispatched to expedite deportation.
Article Summary: Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpuria face more than 25 criminal cases each across Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, including murder. Once the duo deliberately surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and details were fed into US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tracking system.

Article Title: Sourav Ganguly vs 'Doosra': Delhi high court seeks filmmakers’ reply on personality rights plea, asks to arrange screening
Article Text:
The Delhi high court has ordered the makers of 'Doosra' to respond to Sourav Ganguly's plea





NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Friday asked the makers of the film "Doosra" to respond to cricketer Sourav Ganguly's plea alleging violation of his personality rights in the movie, which was released in theatres earlier in the day.A vacation bench of Justice Vinod Kumar said the question of granting interim relief against the film could be decided only after the defendants filed their replies.The court also asked them to arrange a screening of the movie, news agency PTI reported.Justice Kumar, who held court during the high court's Dussehra break, issued summons to the film's producers, director and distributor in the lawsuit filed by Ganguly and Luv Films LLP, which is producing a biopic of the former India captain.The senior counsel representing the defendants submitted that "Doosra" was not a biopic but a fictional story about a middle-class girl from Rajasthan who is inspired by certain sporting events involving Ganguly."(The defendants to make) arrangements for playing the film so that it can be decided whether the personality rights of the plaintiff are violated or not," the court said, listing the matter for hearing on October 29.The defendants' counsel argued that the plea seeking interim relief had become infructuous as the film had already been released. However, the complainant' lawyer contended that a stay could still be granted, PTI reported.On Thursday, the high court had refused to stop the theatrical release of "Doosra" on Ganguly's plea.The senior counsel appearing for the filmmakers had assured the court that the film was not a biopic and that the necessary permissions had been obtained from the appropriate rights holders to use certain clips involving Ganguly.Ganguly's counsel apprehended a violation of the cricketer's personality rights, arguing that no licence had been obtained from him for the production of "Doosra".The defendants' counsel, however, contended that a player cannot claim "personality rights" over clips from the 2002 NatWest series."Doosra: India's Other Freedom Struggle" is a sports drama directed by Abhinay Deo and starring Plabita Borthakur, Ankur Vikal and Samidha Guru.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi high court orders makers of 'Doosra' to respond to Sourav Ganguly's plea. Court also asks them to arrange a screening of the movie. Ganguly had filed a lawsuit alleging violation of his personality rights in movie. Court had refused to stop the theatrical release of " doosra" on Thursday.

Article Title: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
Article Text:
The Supreme Court said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A voter can now not only cast a vote in an election but can also drag an election candidate to court and initiate criminal proceedings for lying and furnishing a false declaration as Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable and the Election Commission’s nod was not needed.Explaining the interplay between Section 125-A of Representation of People Act and Section 195(1) of the CrPC which says that no court shall take cognisance of any offences punishable under sections 172 to 188, including the offence of furnishing false information to a public servant, the top court held that Section 125A of RoP Act does not come within the ambit of Section 195 of CrPC and a court can take cognisance of a private complaint. The court’s ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that “right given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do so”.SC said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002, while Section 195 of CrPC was amended in 2006, and that the omission of the legislature to include Section 125-A of the RoP Act in Section 195 of CrPC was deliberate and no court would be barred from taking cognisance of an alleged offence under Section 125-A of the RoP Act, even on the complaint lodged by a private person.“Should we read into Section 195 of CrPC a prohibition in respect of Section 125-A of the RoP Act also, apart from those expressly included? If indeed it were the intention of the legislature that cognisance of any offence relating to furnishing of false information by a candidate in an affidavit with intent of being elected in an election (referred to in Section 125-A of the RoP Act) could only be taken if the complainant were a public servant, the same could have been provided by an amendment of Section 195, CrPC since Section 125-A of the RoP Act is of fairly recent origin. ”SC also refused to give credence to the EC’s press note that it can take cognisance of such complaints and refer such matters to the relevant investigating authorities on a case-to-case basis. “...Even though the ECI is supreme in its own sphere and has, indeed, issued guidelines/press notes based on its understanding of the statutory provisions, interpretation of statutes is primarily the task of the courts and such guidelines/press notes do not bind us,” the court said.It said that Karnataka HC erred in holding that a private complaint cannot be filed for an offence under Section 125A of RoP Act which is punishable up to six months of jail term. The HC had interpreted the provision solely upon reading the letter issued by the Election Commission of India on the issue which was rejected by the apex court.Allaying the apprehension that allowing the lodging of a criminal complaint by a private person would be misused and frivolous cases would be filed by political rivals, SC said, “If at all a complaint is lodged to harass an elected candidate or frivolous allegations are levelled therein, the laws of the country duly empower the competent magistrates to pass such order(s) as they deem fit and proper commensurate with the facts and circumstances of each case. ”
Article Summary: Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable. The court’s ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.

Article Title: Defer Nov 1 rally, will hit festive business, traders urge Rahul; BJP raps Congress
Article Text:
CTI urged LoP Rahul Gandhi to postpone Congress’s Nov 1 rally.

CEC’s ‘impeachment’ on Oct 30

Nov 1 rally by Rahul to hurt Sikhs: BJP

NEW DELHI: Delhi’s Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged LoP Rahul Gandhi to postpone Congress’s Nov 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Nov 10, citing business disruptions during the peak Diwali shopping season. CTI said the rally could affect market access and traffic for three to four days, potentially impacting Rs 10,000 crore in festive trade.CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said Delhi records Rs 25,000 crore in business on Dhanteras across major sectors. CTI claimed that traders suffered losses of Rs 3,000 crore in Oct due to rallies and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi.INDIA bloc leaders will hold a “public impeachment” of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Oct 30 and announce a public verdict. The “mock Parliament” will be held at Hotel Ashok, where top opposition netas would be present.Congress will be rubbing salt into the wounds of Sikhs by holding an Opposition rally on Nov 1, BJP said Saturday, alleging that the party had started anti-Sikh riots in “collusion” with its then govt on this very day in 1984.BJP claimed some Congress allies have disagreed with Rahul Gandhi’s decision to hold the rally on Nov 1, and said he will be not only hurting the sentiments of Sikhs but also inflicting huge losses on traders as the public meeting will be held during the festive period.“Rahul is irresponsible and indifferent to people’s plight. One can understand his pique with BJP and PM Modi, but is he peeved with people too?” BJP spokesperson Ravi Shankar Prasad askedHe said Congress has a history of downplaying the anti-Sikh riots and denying justice to its victims, recalling Rajiv Gandhi’s statement that the earth shakes when a big tree falls -- referring to his mother Indira Gandhi’s assassination which led to the riots.
Article Summary: CTI urged LoP Rahul Gandhi to postpone Congress’s Nov 1 rally. CTI said the rally could affect market access and traffic for three to four days.CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said Delhi records Rs 25,000 crore in business on Dhanteras.

Article Title: ED moves Supreme Court against HC order to quash case against portal, founder
Article Text:
The Delhi HC had quashed laundering case against news platform NewsClick.

NEW DELHI: Enforcement Directorate has moved Supreme Court against the Delhi high court ’s order quashing the money-laundering case against digital news platform NewsClick and its founder-editor Prabir Purkayastha, alleging that the HC committed a grave error by quashing the 2020 ECIR without examining the allegations against them.The directorate, which filed an appeal almost five months after the HC pronounced the order on May 29, also took the ground that the HC passed the order five months and 26 days after the judgement was reserved and it was in violation of SC’s guidelines that the verdict should be delivered within three months. “That, from a reading of the judgment it appears that due to the lapse of such period in pronouncing the judgment, several critical contentions raised by the prosecution were overlooked or left unaddressed by the high court,” the agency said.Giving details of the financial transaction of the news portal, it said the company was incorporated upon conversion from M/s PP Newsclick Studio LLP on Jan 11, 2018 and within three months, a loss-making company with hardly any assets received FDI worth Rs 9.6 crore by selling its shares for a premium at Rs 11,510/- per share.“PPK’s balance sheet for the FY 2018-19 reveals that it had assets worth only Rs 57 lakhs (approx.) and the company had suffered huge losses varying from Rs 37.8 lakh in FY 2017-18 to Rs.6.61 crore in FY 2018-19. No reason for any genuine investor to pay Rs. 11,510/- per share for a share whose face value was only Rs 10 at the time of allotment only 3 months back,” the appeal said.
Article Summary: The Delhi HC had quashed laundering case against news platform NewsClick. Enforcement Directorate has moved Supreme Court against the Delhi high court ’s order quashing the money-laundering case against NewsClick and its founder- editor. The directorate, which filed an appeal almost five months after the HC pronounced the order on May 29, also took the ground that the HC passed the order five months and 26 days after the judgement was reserved.

Article Title: CBI files FIR against IL&FS Energy, top execs in Rs 212cr Canara Bank loan fraud case
Article Text:
CBI has named M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd, its MD and directors.

NEW DELHI: CBI has registered an FIR against a Mumbaibased firm and its top executives for allegedly cheating Canara Bank of Rs 212 crore, officials said on Saturday. Searches were conducted in Delhi, Mumbai and Noida, and incriminating documents seized.CBI has named M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd, its MD and directors — Sunil Wadhwa, Anoop Seth, Hari Sankaran, Ramesh Chandra Bawa and Arun Kumar Saha — and unknown public servants and private individuals as accused. The case was registered on Oct 21 following a complaint by Canara Bank’s circle office in Bandra.According to CBI, the accused allegedly entered into a conspiracy to secure a term loan of Rs 100 crore from erstwhile Syndicate Bank, now merged with Canara Bank, at its Large Corporate Branch in Mumbai, along with a foreign currency loan of $50 million from its London branch.The company allegedly diverted and siphoned the funds through associate entities instead of using them for sanctioned purposes, causing an estimated wrongful loss of Rs 212.3 crore. The FIR invokes charges of conspiracy, cheating.
Article Summary: CBI has named M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd, its MD and directors. Searches were conducted in Delhi, Mumbai and Noida, and incriminating documents seized. The case was registered on Oct 21 following a complaint by Canara Bank’s circle office in Bandra.

Article Title: Rs 10 lakh cover for 45 paise: Counter rail ticket buyers get insurance option
Article Text:
At present, the optional travel insurance facility is available only for reserved tickets bought online.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From Tuesday (Oct 27), all railway passengers buying reserved tickets from reservation counters can opt for travel insurance. At present, optional travel insurance facility is available only for reserved tickets bought online.The insurance premium is only 45 paise per passenger, including taxes, with coverage of Rs 10 lakh in case of death and permanent total disability in a train accident.The scheme has provision for payment of Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and up to Rs 2 lakh for hospitalisation expenses arising from injuries, as well as Rs 10,000 towards transportation of mortal remains of deceased passengers. The Railway Board has directed all its zones to implement the facility.It said, “Where a passenger opts for insurance, the applicable premium shall be collected along with the ticket fare through digital means only. Staff shall ensure that where the person is opting for insurance, payment is done through digital means.”Reservation staff will inform passengers about the availability of the optional insurance facility and facilitate the exercise of their choice.The board said reservation staff will ensure that the mobile number (mandatory) along with other requisite passenger particulars are captured accurately so as to facilitate transmission of relevant details to the insurance firm for issuance of the policy.Passengers opting for insurance shall be informed that the policy details will be communicated to their registered mobile number.It covers specified railway accidents and untoward incidents, including train collisions, derailments, violent attacks, robbery, arson and accidental falls from trains. Coverage extends to diverted routes and alternative transport arranged by the railways in certain cases of train diversion or short termination.Normal second class or general class passengers are not covered under the insurance policy. It is also not applicable to children below the age of 5 years for whom tickets are issued without a berth or seat. But it is applicable to children in 5-11 age group who have reservation with berth or without berth.
Article Summary: The insurance premium is only 45 paise per passenger, including taxes, with coverage of Rs 10 lakh in case of death and permanent total disability in a train accident. The scheme has provision for payment of Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and up to Rs 2 lakh for hospitalisation expenses arising from injuries.

Article Title: PM Modi to inaugurate RBI's Rs 169-crore data centre in Bhubaneswar, second after Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
RBI's data centre at Jatni would be the second of its kind, after the one in Navi Mumbai (Photo: ANI).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India 's Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar on Sunday, officials said.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi said in a social media post on Saturday that the facility would add to Odisha's development journey. "The visit of the Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modiji to Odisha and the inauguration of RBI's state-of-the-art data centre will not only strengthen the state's digital infrastructure but also give new momentum to the security of the country's financial data and the growth of the digital economy," he said in the post on Saturday.Majhi added that the RBI's data centre at Jatni would be the second of its kind, after the one in Navi Mumbai. The PM last visited the state four months ago, when he attended an event marking two years of the BJP government in Odisha. PTI reported.Officials said the facilities have been designed to meet the central bank's computing requirements and to offer a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the bank and the wider financial sector.According to a government statement, the data centre will house mission-critical payment and settlement systems, besides other flagship initiatives.It will help widen the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services, and will serve as the secure digital foundation on which India's increasingly technology-driven financial economy can grow, the statement said.Similarly, the Cybersecurity Training Institute will strengthen capability building by providing a dedicated institutional platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research and sector-wide capability development, it added.The RBI facility is spread over 18.55 acres. Its foundation stone was laid on March 22, 2023, by the then RBI governor Shaktikanta Das. An official said the site at Info Valley-II was selected for its geographical stability, as it lies away from seismically active zones and high-risk international border areas, thereby reducing exposure to natural disasters and geopolitical vulnerabilities. PTI reportedAs per the schedule, Modi will land at Biju Patnaik International Airport at around 4.10 pm aboard a special Indian Air Force aircraft, officials said. He will then travel by helicopter to Khurda, and from there proceed by road to the RBI facility at Info Valley-II in Jatni.The Prime Minister is expected to spend about an hour at the data centre before returning to the airport by road. He is due to depart at around 6.30 pm.According to PTI, Police have made elaborate security arrangements for the visit, with around 2,100 personnel deployed. Traffic restrictions will also be in force from 5.40 pm to 6.40 pm on the route linking the RBI data centre with the airport.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar on Sunday. Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi said in a social media post on Saturday that the facility would add to Odisha's development journey.

Article Title: Drug trafficking crackdown: Amit Shah hails Operation Trident; Rs 100 crore hawala transactions exposed, 18 arrested
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah

Centre targets drug networks by December 2029

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan reaches over 35 crore people

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday announced a major crackdown on an international narcotics cartel, with Operation Trident targeting 38 locations across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur.The operation, that took place on October 23, uncovered hawala transactions worth Rs 100 crore and resulted in the freezing of 1,424 bank accounts and the attachment of properties valued at Rs 17.82 crore. Officials also seized 500 detonators and Rs 12 lakh in cash, while 18 people were arrested.Announcing the operation on X, Shah said that the cartel was trafficking narcotics across India, Myanmar and Bangladesh through the Death Triangle Corridor. He credited the central agencies and police forces of the three states for the crackdown.“Modi Govt deals another lethal blow against drugs with Operation Trident,” Shah said in his post.He said that the agencies had launched coordinated crackdowns across the three states, dismantling the international network and uncovering its financial transactions. The operation, he added, was part of the Centre's mission to eliminate every drug network in the country by December 31, 2029.“The offensive attests to India’s Himalayan resolve to realise the mission of eradicating every drug network by 31 December 2029. India will hammer until the last nail is driven into the coffin of drug cartels,” Shah said.Congratulating the anti-narcotics team, the home minister acknowledged the role of central agencies and the police forces of Assam, Mizoram and Manipur in the operation.“Heartiest congratulations to the anti-narcotics team comprising central agencies, and police forces of the three states.”The operation comes amid the Centre's push to eliminate drug networks from the country by December 31, 2029. Shah has said that the home ministry will dedicate the remaining part of 2026 and the following three years to freeing the country from the drug menace.He has also called on police forces across the country to participate wholeheartedly in implementing the Nasha Mukt Bharat roadmap.At the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) heads of states and Union territories in New Delhi in September, Shah said the country would collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade by December 31, 2029.He emphasised coordinated action, clear targets and accountability, along with the need to dismantle drug networks. Protecting young people from substance abuse, he said, was also important to achieving the national vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.The Centre's anti-drug efforts also include the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, implemented by the ministry of social justice and empowerment under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).As on date, the campaign has reached more than 35 crore people, including over 13.94 crore young people and 10.86 crore women. It has also engaged with more than 32 lakh educational institutions.Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan initially covered 272 vulnerable districts before expanding its reach across the country. The campaign places particular emphasis on young people, women and communities, recognising their role in preventing substance use and promoting healthy lifestyles.
Article Summary: Operation Trident targeted 38 locations across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur. Officials also seized 500 detonators and Rs 12 lakh in cash. Operation comes amid the Centre's push to eliminate drug networks from the country by December 31, 2029.

Article Title: 'Ignore strike calls': LPG distributor body ahead of Rahul Gandhi's rally in Delhi
Article Text:
The FLDI has urged LPG distributors to continue deliveries, opposing protest and strike calls as Rahul Gandhi’s November 1 rally raises concerns over disruptions in Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Federation of LPG Distributors of India (FLDI) has opposed calls for protests and an indefinite strike in Delhi, urging distributors to continue supply and delivery operations ahead of the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally led by Rahul Gandhi at Ramlila Maidan.In a statement, the distributors' body said it was in talks with oil marketing companies (OMCs) and the petroleum ministry over distributors' demands and had received assurances of an early resolution.The FLDI said protests without exhausting avenues for dialogue were not a practical approach, stressing that uninterrupted LPG supply to consumers remained its priority.Also Read: 'Thanks BJP for promoting': Rahul Gandhi takes swipe at Centre over Nov 1 rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan "We urge all fellow distributors to continue with supply and delivery operations, ignoring unverified calls for action, so that no family faces any inconvenience," the federation said as quoted by news agency ANI.The development comes amid concerns over the impact of the INDIA bloc's rally on Delhi's commercial activity during the festive shopping season."The FLDI does not support the proposed protests and indefinite strike in Delhi. Article Title: ‘PMLA case not examined’: ED moves Supreme Court against HC order quashing proceedings against NewsClick

The case

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has moved the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi high court ’s order quashing a money laundering case against news portal NewsClick and its editor-in-chief, Prabir Purkayastha, over alleged violations of foreign direct investment (FDI) rules.The ED argued that the high court quashed its Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) without examining the merits of the case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). It also flagged a five-month delay in the pronouncement of the judgment.The matter is yet to be listed for hearing.In a judgment dated May 29, Justice Neena Bansal Krishna of the Delhi high court described the continuation of an FIR registered by the Delhi Police’s Economic Offences Wing (EOW) as “nothing but a gross abuse of the process of law”. The judge held that quashing the FIR for the predicate offence also warranted the closure of the ED’s ECIR.The court ruled that the investment was an "economic decision that did not spell out any criminal offence”. Citing the Union ministry of information and broadcasting’s reply to NewsClick, Justice Krishna noted there was no cap or restriction on FDI in digital media at the time.The single-judge bench ruled that the investment followed acceptable practices and that the allegations, even if accepted, did not establish cheating or criminal breach of trust.The alleged victim in the cheating case should have been M/s Worldwide Media Holdings LLC, but the company had filed no complaint. Instead, the complaint came from “merely an informant”.Justice Krishna also rejected the fund-siphoning allegation, noting that a digital media company would naturally incur expenses on salaries, consultation fees and rent.The high court further dismissed the ED’s attempt to sustain the money laundering case on the basis of criminal conspiracy under the IPC, holding that the agency must establish the “illegal objective” or “means” allegedly adopted by NewsClick and others.“Pertinently, extensive investigations were carried out by the ED for about a year and a half, and the petitioners as well as their employees have been summoned and examined many a times, but nothing incriminating till date has been found or placed on record," the order said.“Aside from bald assertions of a criminal conspiracy, there is not a whisper of any incriminating allegation, which would even remotely suggest the commission of the offence punishable under Section 4 of the PMLA,” it added.The bench further stated that the request for a copy of the ECIR had become "infructuous" after the report was quashed.The EOW’s 2020 FIR alleged that PPK Newsclick Studio Pvt Ltd, NewsClick’s parent company, received Rs 9.59 crore in FDI from US-based Worldwide Media Holdings LLC in 2018-19 in violation of foreign investment rules, causing a loss to the government exchequer.It alleged that the company’s shares were grossly overvalued to circumvent the 26% FDI cap for digital news websites, and that over 45% of the investment was siphoned off through salaries, consultation fees and rent for ulterior motives.The ED subsequently registered a money laundering case against NewsClick, Purkayastha and others.PPK Newsclick Studio sought quashing of the FIR, arguing that it contained "vague" allegations.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has moved the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi high court’s order quashing a money laundering case against NewsClick. The ED argued that the high court quashed its Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) without examining the merits of the case. The matter is yet to be listed for hearing.

Article Title: Ashoke Sen: Indian Physicist honoured with 2026 Oskar Klein Medal for string theory work
Article Text:
Ashoke Sen, a distinguished physicist from ICTS, is honored with the prestigious 2026 Oskar Klein Medal.

Contributions to modern string theory

Previous recipients of the Oskar Klein Medal

Physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal, becoming the first physicist from India to receive this honour.Sen, who holds the ICTS-infosys Madhava chair professorship at the International centre for theoretical sciences (ICTS), tata institute of fundamental research (TIFR), Bengaluru, is widely recognised for his pioneering contributions to modern string theory.String theory proposes that the fundamental building blocks of matter are tiny, one-dimensional strings rather than point-like particles. The theory seeks to provide a unified framework for understanding matter and the forces governing interactions between its constituents.Established in 1988, the Oskar Klein Medal is named after Swedish theoretical physicist Oskar Klein. It is awarded annually by stockholm university and the nobel committee for physics of the royal swedish academy of sciences.As part of the oskar klein memorial lectures, a distinguished researcher is invited each year to deliver a lecture in klein's memory and receive the medal.Sen delivered his memorial lecture, titled ‘gravity from strings and strings from gravity’, on October 22 at the AlbaNova university centre in Stockholm.His presentation explored how string theory can provide a consistent quantum description of gravity and help address unresolved questions surrounding the quantum physics of black holes.A recipient of the Padma Shri in 2001 and the Padma Bhushan in 2013, Sen has made several influential theoretical contributions that have helped shape the field of string theory.His work was recognised with the breakthrough prize in fundamental physics in 2012. The research helped establish the idea that different string theories could be understood as distinct limits of a single underlying theory.Congratulating Sen on the achievement, ICTS director Rajesh Gopakumar said, “On behalf of all of us, very warm congratulations to Ashoke. It has been no less than wonderful having Ashoke with us and setting the tone for excellence here at ICTS.”In a statement, ICTS highlighted Sen's internationally recognised contributions to S-duality, the precise counting of black-hole entropy and string field theory, describing them as key areas of work that have helped shape modern string theory.The medal has previously been awarded to several prominent scientists, including Kip Thorne in 2016, Peter Higgs in 2009 and Stephen Hawking in 2003.Other recipients include nobel laureates Hans E. Bethe, who received the medal in 1990; Steven Weinberg, honoured in 1989; and Chen Ning Yang, who was the recipient in 1988.
Article Summary: Physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal. He is the first physicist from India to receive this honour. Sen is widely recognised for his pioneering contributions to modern string theory. His work was recognised with the breakthrough prize in fundamental physics in 2012.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.
