Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: A Baltimore house bought for $43,000 in 2022 was resold for $310,000 in 2023; three years later it was listed for $35,000 after foreclosure as lenders alleged a wider property fraud scheme involving h
Article Text:
How the Baltimore property changed hands

Lenders allege a wider mortgage fraud scheme

The role of investor property loans

Baltimore’s housing market faces the fallout

A Baltimore property that changed hands for $43,000 in 2022 and was resold for $310,000 the following year returned to the market in 2026 for just $35,000 after foreclosure, becoming a striking example of an alleged real estate fraud scheme that has drawn scrutiny from lenders and investigators. In a report published by Realtor dot com on October 20, 2026, journalist Julie Gerstein detailed how two federal lawsuits accuse New York real estate investors Eluzer Gold and Benjamin Eidlisz, along with alleged associates, of inflating property values and securing loans against homes that were subsequently abandoned to foreclosure. The allegations have also featured in reporting by The Baltimore Banner, which investigated the investors’ property acquisitions in the city.The house at 1829 N. Bond Street illustrates the transactions described in the lenders’ complaints. According to the lawsuits, Eidlisz bought the property for $43,000 in May 2022 before selling it in July 2023 to Levy Ventures, a limited liability company linked to Gold, for $310,000.The sharp increase in price allegedly occurred without the renovations that might have justified the higher valuation. The property later went into foreclosure and was listed for $35,000 in August 2026, according to Realtor dot com’s account of the legal filings.The transactions form part of broader allegations involving dozens of properties in Baltimore. Two lenders claim that the investors used companies they controlled to buy distressed homes, transfer them between related entities at substantially higher prices and obtain financing based on allegedly inflated appraisals. Many of the properties subsequently defaulted on their mortgages.Ameritrust Mortgage Corporation filed a federal lawsuit in Maryland on September 9, alleging that Gold, Eidlisz and Shraga Chaim Lerner orchestrated a scheme involving 90 loans worth more than $14 million. The complaint alleges that the loans were obtained with the intention of defaulting on them while retaining the proceeds.A separate lawsuit filed a week later by RCN Capital and Commercial Lender alleges losses of another $10 million involving 59 properties purchased and subsequently defaulted upon between 2023 and 2024. Together, the complaints cover approximately 150 properties, a fraction of the roughly 700 homes the investors were reported to have acquired across the Baltimore area.According to the lenders, shell companies were used to facilitate rapid property transfers, while appraisals allegedly overstated values through inaccurate descriptions, manipulated photographs and other misrepresentations. The complaints contend that lenders would not have approved the financing had the properties been accurately valued. These remain civil allegations, and the lawsuits do not by themselves establish that every named defendant committed fraud.The complaints also draw attention to debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) loans, a financing product commonly used by real estate investors. These loans generally assess a property’s ability to generate sufficient rental income to cover its debt payments, rather than relying primarily on the borrower’s personal income. Such financing can help investors acquire rental properties, but the lawsuits raise questions about the safeguards in place when properties are transferred between related companies and valuations rise sharply over short periods.The alleged scheme depended, in part, on lenders assessing individual transactions without necessarily seeing the full picture of an investor’s holdings and borrowing across multiple entities. If property values were artificially inflated, that could expose lenders to losses when borrowers stopped making payments and the homes entered foreclosure.The allegations have emerged against the backdrop of Baltimore’s longstanding problems with vacant properties, deteriorating housing and housing insecurity. The city’s stock of historic row houses includes many distressed homes, particularly in neighbourhoods where residents have fewer financial resources to absorb sudden disruptions.Foreclosures can have consequences beyond the lenders and property owners involved. Tenants may face uncertainty about their housing, while neglected homes can affect neighbouring properties and complicate efforts to attract legitimate investment for rehabilitation. The Baltimore Banner’s earlier reporting brought attention to the investors’ extensive property acquisitions. An FBI investigation had been reported by The Baltimore Banner, although the FBI declined to confirm or deny its existence when approached by Realtor dot com.The case is not the only example of alleged property-value manipulation in Baltimore. A separate case involving investor Alexander Schultz and attorney Jacob Rappaport resulted in prison sentences earlier in 2026 over a similar scheme involving dozens of homes, according to Realtor dot com. For now, the lawsuits against Gold, Eidlisz and their alleged associates remain part of an ongoing legal process. The $35,000 listing of the Bond Street property offers a visible illustration of the gap between its reported purchase prices and its later market return, while the broader allegations raise questions about property valuations, investor lending and the costs of foreclosure in a city already struggling with distressed housing. The outcome of the lawsuits could also influence how lenders assess property valuations, related-party transactions and risks associated with investor loans in distressed housing markets.
Article Summary: Baltimore property changed hands for $43,000 in 2022 and was resold for $310,000 the following year. The sharp increase in price allegedly occurred without the renovations that might have justified the higher valuation. Two lenders claim that the investors used companies they controlled to buy distressed homes, transfer them between related entities at substantially higher prices and obtain financing based on allegedly inflated appraisals.

Article Title: An Ontario farmer says he turned down a C$16 million offer for his 164-acre fruit farm; instead, his family placed 29 acres under a 999-year easement, with plans to protect the rest from development
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI generated)

A farm built over generations

What a 999-year easement means

Why the land matters beyond the family

A growing model for farmland protection

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the biggest benefit of protecting farmland? Food security Preserving agricultural land Supporting local economies Protecting biodiversity 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

When a developer offered Charles Stevens C$16 million for Wilmot Orchards, the 164-acre fruit farm he helped build near Newcastle, Ontario, he had every reason to consider it. The property sits close to Highway 401 and Lake Ontario, in a rapidly growing part of the Greater Toronto Area where farmland is increasingly attractive for housing and other development. Instead, Stevens and his family chose a very different path. They worked with the Ontario Farmland Trust to place a conservation easement on 29 acres of the farm, legally restricting development for 999 years, and they plan to protect the remaining land in the years ahead. The story has been reported by CBC News, while the Ontario Farmland Trust describes Wilmot Orchards as the first farm in Durham Region protected through its farmland protection programme.The decision was not simply about refusing money. It was about deciding what kind of future the land should have. Wilmot Orchards grows apples and blueberries on some of Canada’s most productive soil, and the Stevens family wanted to ensure that the farm could continue producing food long after the current generation. Their choice turns a private family property into a long-term public commitment to local food, agricultural land and the possibility that future farmers may still afford to work the soil.Charles Stevens bought the land that became Wilmot Orchards in 1975, before graduating from the University of Guelph in 1976. Over the decades, the farm became known for its pick-your-own blueberries as well as its apple orchards, drawing thousands of visitors each summer to pick fruit and spend time in the countryside. Today, it remains both a working farm and a community destination, with the next generation of the Stevens family involved in its operation.The farm occupies Class 1 soil, which the Ontario Farmland Trust identifies as Canada’s most fertile and rarest farmland. Only 0.5 percent of Canada’s landmass is considered Class 1, and more than half of that land is in Ontario. That makes the preservation of places such as Wilmot Orchards especially significant, because the same qualities that make the land excellent for growing food also make it desirable for development.Stevens has watched that pressure grow steadily. The farm’s location, about an hour from Toronto, has brought repeated interest from developers hoping to convert agricultural land into non-farm uses. In interviews and public remarks, he has acknowledged that development is not inherently wrong, but argued that Ontario needs to be smarter about where it builds, particularly when construction threatens scarce high-quality farmland.A conservation easement is a legal agreement attached to the title of a property. It does not necessarily transfer ownership of the land, but it permanently limits certain future uses, in this case preventing the land from being developed for non-agricultural purposes. By placing an easement on Wilmot Orchards, the Stevens family has removed much of the property’s speculative development value while keeping it available for farming.The Ontario Farmland Trust says the family has protected nearly 29 acres of the 164-acre property so far, with plans to protect the rest in the near future. The agreement is designed to last for 999 years, an unusually long horizon that reflects the family’s intention to make the protection effectively permanent. For a farm located in a fast-urbanising region, that legal restriction may matter more than any single owner’s promise to keep it agricultural.Stevens has been candid about the financial trade-off. He told CBC News that a developer once offered him C$16 million for the land, an offer he declined. He has also said that thinking too much about the money involved in placing land in trust could stop a farmer from doing it, explaining that he has never seen anyone take even one dollar to the grave and use it.The protection of Wilmot Orchards has consequences that extend well beyond the Stevens family. Ontario Farmland Trust executive director Martin Straathof described the farm as a promise and a beacon of food security and sovereignty, located on the doorstep of a growing city that needs local food. The easement helps ensure that a productive farm close to a major population centre remains capable of growing fruit rather than becoming another subdivision.The decision also speaks to a wider problem in Canadian agriculture: young and beginning farmers often cannot afford land whose price has been driven up by development potential. Stevens argued that placing farmland in trust is one of the few ways a young farmer in his area might be able to buy land at a farm price, because the easement removes the development premium from the property. In that sense, the family’s action is not only about preserving their own legacy but also about keeping farming economically possible for others.The timing is important. CBC News has reported that Canada has lost millions of hectares of farmland, raising concerns about food security and the future of agriculture near expanding cities. Wilmot Orchards offers one response to that trend: rather than waiting for policy alone to protect farmland, a landowning family used a voluntary legal tool to secure its agricultural future.Wilmot Orchards is the 25th property protected by the Ontario Farmland Trust and its first in Durham Region. With the Stevens farm included, the trust says it has protected more than 2,700 acres across Ontario. The organisation has set a larger goal of reaching 10,000 protected acres by 2029, a target that depends on more landowners choosing similar conservation agreements.The Stevens family’s decision may encourage other farmers facing similar offers to consider easements as an option. It does not erase the financial pressures of farming, nor does it solve every challenge facing agriculture in Ontario. But it demonstrates that a farm can be treated as more than real estate waiting for a higher and better use.For now, Wilmot Orchards continues to grow apples and blueberries, welcome visitors and employ the knowledge of several generations. Its future is no longer dependent only on market pressures or the intentions of one family. Through a 999-year easement, the Stevens family has written their choice into the land itself, ensuring that this fertile corner of Ontario remains a farm rather than another development site. The agreement also offers a potential example for other landowners seeking to balance financial opportunities with long-term agricultural preservation as development pressure continues to grow around Ontario's urban centres.
Article Summary: Charles Stevens helped build Wilmot Orchards, a 164-acre fruit farm near Newcastle, Ontario. He and his family worked with the Ontario Farmland Trust to place a conservation easement on 29 acres of the farm, restricting development for 999 years. The farm occupies Class 1 soil, which is considered Canada’s most fertile and rarest farmland.

Article Title: An Illinois mansion had $8.75 million in insurance coverage after a fire, but its owner received just $25,000 for most contents used in a wedding and lodging business
Article Text:
Representative Image of a grand mansion engulfed in flames, with lightning striking in the background, symbolizing destruction and loss (AI-generated image)

How Pine Manor became a wedding venue and luxury lodging business

Why Chubb paid $8.75 million for the house but only $25,000 for its contents

What the Seventh Circuit decided in Gibson v. Chubb National Insurance Company

A lightning strike destroyed Pine Manor, a 24,000-square-foot mansion in southern Illinois, in October 2019, leaving owner Wesley Gibson facing a dispute over insurance coverage for the antiques, artwork and furnishings inside. His homeowner’s policy with Chubb National Insurance Company covered the building for $8.75 million and its contents for $3.5 million. Chubb paid the full amount for the house but limited the contents payout to $25,000, arguing that most of the property had been used to operate a commercial lodging and events venue. Gibson challenged the decision, saying the policy should cover his collection of personal belongings. On July 13, 2026, the US Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit upheld the insurer’s position in Gibson v. Chubb National Insurance Company. The court concluded that most of the mansion’s contents were used to conduct Gibson’s business and fell under the policy’s business-property limit. The ruling turned on the policy’s wording and how the contents were used, rather than when or why they had been acquired.Gibson bought Pine Manor in the late 1990s as a vacation home for his family.Located on a private lake in the foothills of the Shawnee National Forest near Carbondale, Illinois, the 24,000-square-foot mansion was gradually transformed into a commercial lodging and events complex. Gibson spent millions renovating the property and furnishing it with family heirlooms, artwork and antiques, including an Italian rococo-style mirror and windows from the original Lloyd’s of London building. The estate eventually expanded to almost a dozen structures across more than 100 wooded acres. Its amenities included conference facilities, a pool, a carriage house, a boat dock and sports courts. Gibson also acquired neighbouring properties to accommodate additional guests and marketed Pine Manor as a luxury country inn and resort.The business generated substantial income. Between 2016 and 2019, Gibson’s consulting firm paid a $70,000 monthly retainer to use the estate for corporate training retreats, which could occupy up to 20 weeks each year. Pine Manor also hosted between 6 and 16 weddings annually, according to the court’s opinion. In both 2017 and 2018, the estate earned about $1 million in lodging revenue. Gibson’s tax returns reported 365 fair-rental days. Although Gibson and his family continued to stay at Pine Manor for about 70 nights a year, the property’s primary use had shifted to commercial accommodation and events. The estate held the relevant licences for its operations, and Gibson employed an on-site property manager and approximately 10 other full-time workers for housekeeping and landscaping. On October 22, 2019, lightning struck the mansion and started a fire while the property was unoccupied. The house and its contents were deemed a total loss, but nobody was injured.Pine Manor was insured under Chubb’s Masterpiece homeowner’s policy. Its Deluxe House section provided approximately $8.75 million in coverage for the building, while the Deluxe Contents section provided $3.5 million for personal property. The distinction between the two sections became central to the dispute. The building coverage did not contain the business-property exclusion at issue in the case, so Chubb paid the full $8.75 million policy limit for the mansion. The contents coverage, however, excluded losses involving business property, subject to an additional coverage provision that capped payment for such property at $25,000.The policy defined business property to include furniture, equipment, inventory, records and other items used to conduct the insured’s business. It covered activities intended to generate financial gain, whether conducted full time, part time or occasionally. Chubb argued that Gibson had used the contents of Pine Manor to operate his lodging and events business. The insurer therefore paid the $25,000 limit rather than the full $3.5 million contents amount.The dispute was not entirely unexpected. In June 2017, a Chubb underwriter had identified a potential gap in coverage after discovering that Pine Manor was no longer being used solely as a private residence. The underwriter warned Gibson’s insurance broker and recommended switching to commercial property insurance. Gibson nevertheless renewed the homeowner’s policy in 2018 and 2019. Gibson sued Chubb for breach of contract and alleged violations of the Illinois Insurance Code and the Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act. He sought the full contents coverage, arguing that the policy should not classify his personal furnishings and antiques as business property merely because the mansion hosted paying guests.The district court ruled that most contents were subject to the $25,000 limit, except items in areas inaccessible to guests, including a wine cellar, a gun safe and 2 locked master-bedroom closets. The Seventh Circuit affirmed the district court’s decision in an opinion written by Judge Diane S. Sykes. It agreed that the policy’s definition of business property included furnishings and decorations used to conduct the lodging and events business, not just conventional office equipment. The court described the district judge’s interpretation as “exactly right,” concluding that the policy’s broad definition of business extended to property used in activities intended to generate financial gain. The court pointed to the role the mansion’s collection played in attracting guests and shaping their experience. Pine Manor’s website advertised its art and antiques as part of the estate’s appeal, and guests could access and use most of the furnishings and collections throughout the mansion. The court concluded that these items helped conduct the business. Gibson also argued that many items had been acquired before Pine Manor became a commercial venue and continued to serve personal purposes when his family visited. The court rejected that argument, explaining that the policy focused on how the contents were used when the loss occurred, not when or why they were purchased.The court also rejected Gibson’s argument that property qualified as business property only if it was used entirely for commercial purposes. It agreed with the district court that the policy covered property used “whether partially or fully” to conduct the business. The policy’s wording, including a provision addressing property used “in whole or in part” for business purposes, supported that interpretation. The court left open the narrower question of whether de minimis, or negligible, business use would be enough to trigger the exclusion. It did not decide that every instance of occasional business use automatically makes personal property ineligible for broader coverage. The Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for Chubb on Gibson’s statutory claims under the Illinois Insurance Code and the Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act. The claim under Section 155 of the Illinois Insurance Code failed because a genuine dispute over coverage existed and Chubb had conducted a reasonable investigation. The Consumer Fraud Act claim also failed because Chubb’s coverage decision followed the policy’s plain terms. The court described the dispute as “not just genuine; it was justified” and said the district judge’s interpretation of the policy was “exactly right.”
Article Summary: A lightning strike destroyed Pine Manor, a 24,000-square-foot mansion in southern Illinois, in October 2019. Owner Wesley Gibson faced a dispute over insurance coverage for the antiques, artwork and furnishings inside. His homeowner’s policy with Chubb National Insurance Company covered the building for $8.75 million and its contents for $3.5 million. Chubb paid the full amount for the house but limited the contents payout to $25,000. Gibson challenged the decision, saying the policy should cover his collection of personal belongings. Article Title: Maternity leave no excuse for unapproved absence: Karnataka high court
Article Text:
Karnataka HC clarified that while maternity leave offers essential protections, it does not allow for excessive unauthorized leave

QUOTE:





BENGALURU: Maternity leave cannot shield an employee from the consequences of prolonged unauthorised absence after the approved leave period expires, Karnataka high court has observed while dismissing a petition by one of its former employees.In the judgment delivered on Oct 16, Justice M Nagaprasanna held that statutory maternity protections must be respected, but cannot be invoked to invalidate action taken against absence beyond permissible leave period.The petitioner was appointed as a software technician at the high court on June 6, 2019. She applied for maternity leave on July 1, 2023, and later sought an extension until Aug 14, 2024. On Sept 25, 2024, the principal district judge of Bengaluru Rural district, under whom she was on probation, directed her to report for duty.In response, she said she could not resume work because no one was available to look after her newborn. Citing her ill health, she also sought a further extension of leave.On April 15, 2025, the registrar general dismissed her from service for failing to report for duty. Challenging the order, she approached the high court, contending that the order to dismiss her was in violation of law.The court, however, observed that the petitioner could not treat public employment casually, adding that she had been granted all permissible forms of leave under the law.The judge further noted that at a time when countless qualified aspirants compete for limited public service opportunities, an employee cannot treat such a privilege it with indifference.The court noted that public employment also carried certain responsibilities. “The petitioner cannot seek to draw sustenance from a right, which was never denied to her, to invalidate an action founded upon circumstances arising independently thereafter,” Justice Nagaprasanna observed while dismissing the petition.“An appointment to public service cannot be regarded as a privilege to be enjoyed at convenience and an obligation to be discharged at leisureJustice M Nagaprasanna | Karnataka HC
Article Summary: Karnataka high court dismissed a petition by one of its former employees. Justice M Nagaprasanna held that statutory maternity protections must be respected, but cannot be invoked to invalidate action taken against absence beyond permissible leave period. The court noted that public employment also carried certain responsibilities.

Article Title: IMD predicts wet spell for Bengaluru over next 2 days
Article Text:
Bengaluru and its neighboring areas are bracing for heavy rain as two weather systems emerge





BENGALURU: With twin weather systems intensifying over Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal, Bengaluru and adjoining districts of south-interior Karnataka are likely to receive fairly widespread rain until Tuesday, according to India Meteorological Department.Meteorologists told TOI a well-marked low-pressure area over southeast Arabian Sea and adjoining Lakshadweep region may to intensify into a depression by Sunday morning.Meanwhile, another low-pressure system over Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday morning before moving towards Andhra Pradesh coast by Wednesday."Bengaluru and adjoining districts of Mysuru, Kodagu and Chamarajanagar could experience spells of rain until Tuesday under the influence of these twin weather systems. Rainfall is likely to be fairly widespread until Monday, before easing to isolated spells rest of the week. However, cloudy and occasionally windy conditions are likely to prevai," said CS Patil, a scientist at IMD, Bengaluru.
Article Summary: Bengaluru and adjoining districts of south-interior Karnataka are likely to receive fairly widespread rain until Tuesday. Two weather systems are intensifying over Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal. Rainfall is likely to be fairly widespread until Monday, before easing to isolated spells rest of the week.

Article Title: Bengaluru leads post-SIR voter activity as form 6 applications rise 32%
Article Text:
Bengaluru experienced a significant rise in voter applications for inclusion and deletion following the special intensive revision deadline.

Bengaluru leads in voter applications as deletion requests jump 291%

Bengaluru’s low re-entry





BENGALURU: Bengaluru recorded Karnataka ’s highest number of applications for inclusion, deletion and correction of voter details after the special intensive revision (SIR) claims deadline, even as Form 6 applications rose 32.4% and deletion requests surged 291.48% across the state.Karnataka received 2.6 lakh Form 6 applications seeking inclusion in electoral rolls between Sept 23 and Oct 22.Form 7 applications seeking deletions or objecting to inclusions rose by 1.7 lakh, while 2.1 lakh Form 8 applications were filed for corrections and address changes, up 19.2% during the past one month.Bengaluru Urban topped Form 6 applications with 26,654, followed by Belagavi (17,437) and BBMP South (13,755), North (12,070) and Central (11,719) zones. Deletion requests were the highest in Bengaluru Urban (21,999), BBMP South (18,578) and BBMP North (17,471), followed by Dakshina Kannada (8,255) and Tumakuru (6,707).Bengaluru Urban also led Form 8 applications with 12,255, followed by Belagavi (11,680), Dakshina Kannada (11,487), Vijayanagara (9,051) and Mysuru (9,021), according to CEO office data.Bengaluru’s voter base of 1.03 crore before SIR saw a large number of electors marked absent, shifted, dead, duplicate or otherwise categorised (ASDDO) in the draft rolls.During the claims and objections period from Aug 24 to Sept 23, the region received only 2.2 lakh Form 6 applications for inclusion — around 5% of the ASDDO count.The CEO’s office has not disclosed how many applicants were new voters, leaving it unclear how many excluded electors sought re-entry. Karnataka’s draft rolls recorded 1.07 crore ASDDO deletions, most of them in Bengaluru. Districts outside Bengaluru accounted for about 4 lakh deletions but submitted 5.6 lakh of the state’s 7.7 lakh Form 6 applications during the claims period.
Article Summary: Karnataka received 2.6 lakh Form 6 applications seeking inclusion in electoral rolls between Sept 23 and Oct 22. Form 7 applications seeking deletions or objecting to inclusions rose by 1.7 lakh. 2.1 lakh Form 8 applications were filed for corrections and address changes, up 19.2% during the past one month.

Article Title: IMD issues heavy to very heavy rain in Tamil Nadu; red alert for Nilgiris, orange alert for 9 districts
Article Text:
The India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in Nilgiris district and nearby areas

Rainfall forecast for 24th of October for Tamil Nadu





CHENNAI: The IMD on Saturday issued a red alert for the Nilgiris district, warning of extremely heavy rainfall. Several other parts of Tamil Nadu, along with Puducherry and Karaikal, are also likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall.According to the Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai, the Nilgiris is expected to receive extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 204.4 mm.An orange alert has been issued for Coimbatore, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, Kallakurichi, Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur and Nagapattinam, as well as Puducherry and Karaikal. These areas are likely to receive 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm of rainfall.A yellow alert has been issued for Tiruvallur, Chennai, Ranipet, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Vellore, Tirupattur, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri, Erode, Salem, Namakkal, Tiruppur, Karur, Tiruchirappalli, Perambalur, Ariyalur, Dindigul, Pudukkottai, Theni, Madurai, Sivaganga, Ramanathapuram and Kanniyakumari, where rainfall of 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm is forecast.Moderate rainfall of 15.6 mm to 64.4 mm is expected in Virudhunagar, Tenkasi, Thoothukudi and Tirunelveli districts.Residents in vulnerable areas, particularly hilly areas of the Nilgiris and low-lying coastal regions, have been advised to follow official weather updates and avoid unnecessary travel in areas under red and orange alerts.District administrations have been asked to take precautionary measures against possible waterlogging and landslides.
Article Summary: The India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in Nilgiris district and nearby areas. Several other parts of Tamil Nadu, along with Puducherry and Karaikal, are also likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall.

Article Title: CM Devendra Fadnavis announces mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port, seeks Centre’s nod for 2,500-5,000 acres in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has revealed plans for a significant chemical park adjacent to Vadhvan Port





MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has announced plans for a mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port and urged the Centre to approve the project, for which the state government is willing to allot between 2,500 and 5,000 acres.Speaking at the inauguration of Indochem in Goregaon, Fadnavis said the state government would make the land available for the proposed park and asked the Centre to sanction the project.The proposed location is significant as Dahanu taluka in Palghar district was previously designated an ecologically sensitive zone.Union minister for chemicals and fertilisers JP Nadda said the Centre had already announced the Bhavya Rasayan scheme in the Union Budget. Under the scheme, the Centre will provide Rs 1,000 crore, while the state government will contribute Rs 500 crore.Nadda said the Centre would facilitate environmental clearances for the scheme.The proposed initiative is part of the Centre’s Viksit Bharat vision and its goal of building a $1 trillion economy by 2040.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis has announced plans for a mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port. The state government is willing to allot between 2,500 and 5,000 acres for the project. The proposed location is significant as Dahanu taluka in Palghar district was previously designated an ecologically sensitive zone.

Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: Google’s Ex-CEO Eric Schmidt sees China behind the US in the AI race by at least 6 months, but is still impressed by Chinese …
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt ‘If they’re six months behind, we’re already losing’

Google’s ex-CEO points to smuggled chips and AI distillation

AI is not a bubble, says Eric Schmidt

Price may matter more than performance

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months, but he warns that the gap may not guarantee an American win. Talking about the intensifying global AI competition, Schmidt said that China is only about six months behind the US in AI capabilities. Along with this, he also warned that the country’s focus on making low-cost and free AI products could enable it to dominate the global adoption. Schmidt believes that if the Chinese AI companies continue to offer powerful AI models at little of no cost, then they could easily gain a huge and significant advantage in developing markets which will incur pressure on the business model of leading AI companies in the US.As reported by Benzinga, speaking on the In Good Company podcast hosted by Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management, Schmidt said China's position in the AI race is much stronger than many in the West may believe. He argued that even if Chinese AI firms remain slightly behind the technological frontier, their strategy of offering inexpensive or free AI services could help them win users at a global scale.“I don’t know that they will get ahead, but I will tell you that if they’re six months behind, then we’re already losing because their strategy is that the products are free,” Schmidt said.Schmidt noted that many Chinese AI models are either free or significantly cheaper than their Western counterparts.Combined with the growing popularity of open-weight models, this pricing strategy could make Chinese AI offerings particularly attractive in emerging economies where businesses and consumers may not be able to afford premium AI subscriptions.The former Google chief also discussed how China has rapidly reduced the AI gap despite US export restrictions on advanced semiconductor technology. Schmidt said some of China's progress may have been enabled by access to cutting-edge chips that the country was “not supposed to have,” suggesting that some hardware may have been “pilfered or smuggled” into the country.Another factor, he said, is the use of AI distillation techniques, in which developers query advanced AI systems and use the generated responses to train their own models. Such approaches, combined with software innovation, have helped Chinese companies narrow what was once viewed as a much larger technological gap.Schmidt has previously said that China was one to two years behind the US in AI development. He now believes the gap has shrunk to less than six months, highlighting the speed at which Chinese AI firms have progressedDespite growing concerns over the massive sums being invested in artificial intelligence, Schmidt dismissed suggestions that the industry is experiencing a speculative bubble. The technology investor, who owns a stake in Anthropic, argued that the sector's financial performance demonstrates real customer demand rather than hype-driven growth.Pointing to Anthropic's rapid expansion, Schmidt said the company has achieved revenue growth at a pace that exceeds what Google experienced during his tenure as CEO.“That’s real growth. It’s not fake. It’s real money, with real customers who are paying for something useful,” he said.Schmidt's comments come amid an increasingly common view in the AI industry that affordability could become a bigger competitive factor than having the absolute most advanced model. While frontier AI systems continue to grab headlines, many businesses are primarily interested in practical tools that deliver acceptable performance at a reasonable cost.To illustrate the point, Schmidt highlighted a WeChat AI agent developed by Tencent Holdings that can scan medicine packaging and quickly provide personalised guidance. The example, he said, shows how AI systems do not necessarily need to be the most sophisticated models available to deliver meaningful value to users.He added that businesses evaluating AI investments often compare the cost of adopting AI tools with the cost of hiring additional employees, making pricing a critical consideration for enterprise adoption.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months. But he warns that the gap may not guarantee an American win. Schmidt said China's focus on making low-cost and free AI products could enable it to dominate the global adoption.

Article Title: Snapchat billionaire Evan Spiegel and wife Miranda Kerr help erase $550 million in medical debt for 261,000 Californians struggling to pay bills, now turning to LA wildfire survivors
Article Text:
Image: Evan Spiegel/ Instagram

Snapchat billionaire helps erase $550 million in medical debt

Spiegel turns to Los Angeles wildfire recovery

Department of Angels supports wildfire survivors

Couple fund research into long-term health effects of the fires

Spiegel and Kerr involve their children in charitable work

Evan Spiegel honoured for philanthropy in Washington

Snapchat co-founder and Snap Inc. CEO Evan Spiegel and his wife, Australian model and entrepreneur Miranda Kerr, have helped erase $550 million in medical debt owed by more than 261,000 Californians. The couple made a multimillion-dollar donation to Undue Medical Debt, a nonprofit that purchases qualifying medical debt for a fraction of its original value before cancelling it. Their philanthropic efforts also extend to Los Angeles, where devastating wildfires in January 2025 destroyed thousands of structures, including Spiegel’s childhood home in Pacific Palisades. More than a year after the disaster, the couple continues to support recovery initiatives for affected residents and research into the fires’ long-term health consequences. Spiegel was honoured for his philanthropic work at an awards ceremony in Washington, DC, on October 13, 2026.Spiegel and Kerr’s medical debt relief initiative was announced in June 2026 and reported by the Los Angeles Times. Their contribution helped Undue Medical Debt cancel more than $550 million in outstanding medical bills for over 261,000 Californians.The nonprofit acquires medical debt in bulk from hospitals, physician groups, collection agencies and other creditors, often paying substantially less than the original amount owed.It then cancels the acquired debt, allowing eligible individuals to receive relief without having to repay the outstanding balance.According to the organisation, people generally qualify if their household income is at or below 400% of the federal poverty level or if their medical debt represents at least 5% of their annual income. Recipients do not need to apply individually because the nonprofit identifies and purchases qualifying debts in bulk.The $550 million figure represents the face value of the debt cancelled, rather than the amount donated by the couple. Their precise contribution has not been publicly disclosed.The initiative reached communities across California. San Diego County received approximately $99 million in medical debt relief, benefiting 40,369 people, while Los Angeles County saw $26.7 million in debt cancelled for 17,466 residents, according to figures reported by the Los Angeles Times.The couple’s philanthropy has also focused on communities devastated by the January 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles County. Spiegel grew up in Pacific Palisades, where his childhood home was destroyed during the disaster.The fires killed dozens of people and destroyed more than 16,000 structures, according to early assessments. The destruction left thousands of residents facing the lengthy process of securing assistance, assessing damage and rebuilding their homes.The disaster also affected Spiegel’s company. In an interview with PEOPLE published on October 15, 2026, he said more than 100 Snap employees had been affected by the fires.In January 2025, Spiegel, Snap and Snapchat co-founder Bobby Murphy contributed $5 million in immediate aid. The support formed part of a wider philanthropic response to the disaster.Recalling the moment he learnt that his childhood home was burning, Spiegel told PEOPLE that his sister alerted the family after seeing the house on television. He described the experience as surreal, particularly because the house was where he and Murphy had started Snapchat.Spiegel also helped launch the Department of Angels, a nonprofit established to support Los Angeles wildfire recovery. The California Community Foundation, Snap, Spiegel and Murphy committed a combined $10 million in seed funding to establish the initiative, the Los Angeles Times reported.The organisation works to connect affected residents with resources, support community-led recovery and bring survivors’ concerns to decision-makers at the local, state and federal levels.Its work comes as many residents continue to face obstacles in rebuilding their homes and returning to their neighbourhoods. In August 2026, The Guardian reported that thousands of wildfire survivors were still waiting for more than $15 billion in federal recovery assistance.Spiegel told PEOPLE that the delays remained frustrating and stressed that the recognition of his philanthropic work should not overshadow the needs of affected communities.Beyond immediate financial assistance, the Spiegel Family Fund supported the launch of the Los Angeles Fire Human Exposure and Long-Term Health Study, also known as the L.A. Fire HEALTH Study, in January 2025.The 10-year research initiative brings together scientists from institutions including UCLA, Harvard University, the University of California, Davis, and the University of Texas at Austin. Researchers are investigating pollutants released during the fires, how they spread through air, soil, dust and water, and the possible short- and long-term health consequences of exposure.The study also aims to provide evidence that can help residents understand the risks of returning to affected homes and neighbourhoods. Urban fires can burn synthetic materials, household products and building components, potentially releasing a complex mixture of pollutants.The findings could help communities better prepare for future urban wildfires and guide decisions about environmental monitoring and recovery. Researchers will need to follow exposed populations over time to establish the nature and extent of any lasting health effects.The couple have also sought to make community service part of family life. Spiegel and Kerr are raising three sons together, Hart, Myles and Pierre. Kerr also has a son, Flynn, from her previous marriage to actor Orlando Bloom.Speaking to PEOPLE, Spiegel said the family tries to involve their children in activities such as packing meals and baking cookies for a local women's shelter.He said he wants his children to understand that their opportunities come with a responsibility to help people who are less fortunate. Kerr, he added, has inspired him through her care for others since the early days of their relationship.Their philanthropic interests extend beyond medical debt and disaster recovery. In 2022, the couple helped pay off student loans for the graduating class at Otis College of Art and Design in Los Angeles. Spiegel's wider giving also includes support for creative education and opportunities for young people through the Spiegel Family Fund and the Snap Foundation.On October 13, 2026, Spiegel was honoured at the eighth annual George H.W. Bush Points of Light Awards in Washington, DC. The ceremony recognised individuals for their philanthropic work, volunteering and contributions to communities across the United States.Other honourees included David M. Rubenstein, co-founder of investment firm The Carlyle Group, and Olivia Zhang, founder and CEO of Cancer Kids First.Reflecting on the recognition, Spiegel told PEOPLE that he was grateful for what had been accomplished but believed it was important to acknowledge how much more work remained. He specifically pointed to wildfire survivors still waiting for federal assistance.He also spoke about the importance of helping others, describing people as interconnected and saying that this creates an obligation to support one another. For Spiegel and Kerr, their efforts span immediate financial relief for families burdened by medical bills and longer-term work to help communities recover from disasters.
Article Summary: Snap Inc. CEO Evan Spiegel and his wife Miranda Kerr have helped erase $550 million in medical debt owed by more than 261,000 Californians. The couple made a multimillion-dollar donation to Undue Medical Debt, a nonprofit that purchases qualifying medical debt for a fraction of its original value. Their philanthropic efforts also extend to Los Angeles, where devastating wildfires in January 2025 destroyed thousands of structures, including Spiegel’s childhood home.
